questions.stem: A cyclist travels 840 m in 60 seconds. What is the cyclist's average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = distance / time = 840 / 60 = 14 m/s. Option (a) divides time by distance instead. Option (d) multiplies distance by time. Always check your rearrangement: speed = distance ÷ time.

questions.stem: A runner completes a 200 m straight race in 25 seconds, running due north. What is the runner's average velocity?
questions.explanation: Average velocity = displacement / time = 200 m north / 25 s = 8 m/s north. Since this is a straight race, displacement equals distance. Option (a) gives speed (no direction), not velocity. Velocity is a vector, so a direction must always be stated.

questions.stem: A car travels at 108 km/h. What is this speed in m/s?
questions.explanation: To convert km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6: 108 ÷ 3.6 = 30 m/s. Option (d) multiplies by 3.6 instead of dividing — that would convert m/s to km/h. Option (a) divides by 10, which is incorrect. The factor 3.6 comes from: 1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s, so 1000/3600 = 1/3.6.

questions.stem: A dog runs 80 m east in 10 s, then 80 m west in 10 s, returning to its starting position. What are the average speed and average velocity for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time = (80 + 80) / (10 + 10) = 160/20 = 8 m/s. Average velocity = total displacement / total time = 0/20 = 0 m/s (the dog returns to its start, so displacement is zero). This shows a key difference: average speed uses distance; average velocity uses displacement.

questions.stem: Sound travels at approximately 340 m/s. During a thunderstorm, a student sees lightning and hears thunder 4 seconds later. How far away is the storm?
questions.explanation: Using distance = speed × time: d = 340 × 4 = 1360 m. Light travels almost instantaneously, so the delay is due to the time sound takes to reach the student. Option (b) forgets to multiply by the time. Option (a) divides speed by time instead of multiplying.
